acceptance_evidence: AC1, sync generates both copies and doctor fails on a hand edit: eight tests in test_skill.py, and doctor on this tree reports nothing
AC2, the skill is where each assistant looks: sync wrote all three paths including ~/.codex/skills/seen-harness/SKILL.md, and each copy carries the frontmatter an assistant reads
AC3, no Seene leftover remains: already true, because the project was removed in SEEN-086's first commit and the history rebuilt from a fresh root. Recorded at record 2 rather than claimed as work
AC4, CLAUDE.md links the workflow and lists the commands as they now are: the list gained coverage, lint, discard, reopen, verify-merge and sync, and lost nothing that does not exist
AC5, this ticket's journal is the reference example, with its kpi.json committed and the skill pointing at it
The workflow document describes the harness as built: the command table, the modules, what sits outside the fingerprint, and the five conventions the ten tickets settled

findings.claim: Adding a check to doctor broke every test project, because the fixture had nothing for it to check
findings.failure_scenario: Ten tests failed on a self-check finding a missing skill source in a project that never had one. The same gap as the pre-commit hook in SEEN-090: a fixture that does not carry the controls cannot exercise them, and the failure looks like a defect in the check
findings.resolution: The fixture generates the source and both copies the same way sync does, so the drift check is exercised rather than skipped

findings.claim: The Codex copy lives outside the repository, so doctor cannot see it drift
findings.failure_scenario: Someone edits ~/.codex/skills/seen-harness/SKILL.md, no check notices, and Codex reads something different from what Claude Code reads
findings.resolution: sync rewrites it whenever it runs, and the ticket and the workflow document both say the check covers the committed copies only. A self-check that failed on another machine's configuration would be noise, and claiming coverage that does not exist would be worse than naming the limit

findings.claim: Two acceptance criteria were satisfied before the ticket started
findings.failure_scenario: A reader takes the ticked boxes as work done here and looks for commits that do not exist
findings.resolution: Both say what made them true and when. The Seene removal happened in SEEN-086's first commit; the allowlist came from SEEN-090

security_checklist: sync writes outside the repository only into a directory that already exists, and never creates one
No live marketplace host in any test file
No PII, no database, no agent action
